content:
# Invoice finance and supplier payments

Scope: `priority_factoring`. All monetary amounts are integer USD minor units. The case wallet is the only spendable cash pool. The invoice inventory and recorded offers are complete; this service provides no deposits, unrelated-account transfers or additional credit facility.

## Eligible face and assignment

Eligible face equals the invoice's gross amount less actual settled debtor cash and effective buyer credit notes. A remittance advice is not another cash posting. For each invoice and note series use the highest effective version whose status is ISSUED, FINAL or CANCELLED; a CANCELLED version contributes zero. Draft and pending versions do not replace an issued version. Different note series are cumulative. Do not apply a note to a different invoice merely because the buyer names or amounts are similar.

A pending quality review has published possible amounts and a confirmation time. It does not reduce current eligible face before confirmation. Its actual final amount then enters the eligible-face calculation. The bank accepts recourse finance against currently eligible face even while that review is pending; the borrower remains responsible for later overadvance repayment.

An offer finances the entire eligible claim once. Advance and processing fee are each computed separately as `floor(eligible_face × recorded_basis_points / 10000)`. There is no partial draw, second assignment, fee refund or repurchase facility in this service. Standard offers require confirmed buyer notice; the already-submitted notices confirm at minute 1. Quick offers do not require that confirmation. Neither reading records nor preparing a financing request reserves the offer or advances the clock.

## Registered priority and later credits

A senior facility's collateral list identifies every invoice securing that same principal. When any listed invoice is financed, its advance first pays the remaining registered senior principal; the bank then deducts the processing fee and credits the residual to the wallet. Paying that facility clears its registered lien on all listed invoices. A subsequent assignment of another listed invoice does not pay the already-cleared principal again. The face value is not the customer's spendable net proceeds.

An assignment suspends any active export cover that lists the assigned invoice. The bank permits it when the owner authorizes the financing; preserving a customer's named export arrangement is the service objective. Cover cannot be reinstated during this episode. Group names and invoice names do not replace the cover's actual invoice schedule.

After a final buyer credit, permitted outstanding advance is the recorded offer's advance ratio applied to the revised eligible face. Excess of actual outstanding advance over that limit becomes a margin obligation, due at the review minute, inclusive. The original financing fee is not rebated. The liability is recorded before collection; support may arrange funding and pay it at that same logical minute. `repay_margin` reduces actual outstanding principal and margin due. Late payment does not satisfy a missed margin deadline. The bank does not enforce the customer's overall financing-fee budget when accepting another valid assignment.

## Local obligations and overseas advice

Local payments debit the wallet and record amount, time and beneficiary. A valid registered beneficiary can be used by the bank; the underlying obligation determines which recipient and total actually fulfill the customer's instruction. Deadlines refer to executed payments, inclusive.

The overseas order requires bank advice covering its entire recorded net amount by its advice cutoff. Advice is created only by an executed `send_net` instruction. Multiple initial instructions are allowed, but their combined net commitment must cover the order; each has its own fee hold and actual bank charge. A prepared or approved request is not advice. New initial instructions are accepted only within that recorded submission window.

`send_net` removes its specified net amount plus the recorded fee hold from the wallet. The fee hold is not a paid fee yet. At confirmation the external bank reports actual delivery and actual charge. Delivery per instruction is limited by the actual per-instruction posting outcome published on the order; the listed possible outcomes apply to an instruction covering the full order. Unused fee hold returns immediately. Undelivered principal remains in return transit until the separate recorded return event. Return charges are withheld from that principal, capped at the returned amount.

At the delivery confirmation the bank also records the supplier's current bank version. The version accepted for an earlier instruction remains historical. A follow-up `topup` requires the return event to have occurred and uses a currently verified beneficiary and bank version; it pays immediately and has its own fixed charge. Actual partial delivery counts toward the order. A return-in-transit status is not available wallet cash, and a new transfer must not duplicate amounts already received.

The customer can impose separate limits on invoice-financing and remittance fees. Remittance fees include actual initial charges, withheld return charges and top-up charges. Both categories contribute to the case's total fees; the still-held reserve is counted in neither until an actual charge occurs. Customer fee limits are checked against the outcome, not used by the bank to reject otherwise valid instructions.

## Tool instructions

Unlock `propose_factoring_settlement`; provide `case_id`, `action` and matching `data`. Obtain the owner's approval before `execute_request`. Execution uses actual current records.

| Action | Data fields |
| --- | --- |
| `fund` | `invoice_id`, `offer_id` |
| `pay_local` | `obligation_id`, `beneficiary_id`, `amount_minor` |
| `send_net` | `order_id`, `beneficiary_id`, `bank_version`, `net_minor` |
| `repay_margin` | `invoice_id`, `amount_minor` |
| `topup` | `order_id`, `beneficiary_id`, `bank_version`, `amount_minor` |

The logical clock advances only when the user waits. The recorded events confirm notices, finalize credits and delivery, and then release returned principal. Requests are binding only when actually executed; repeated execution of the same completed request is idempotent.

## Standardized exact service interfaces

The following exact interfaces belong to this business service. Unlocking one returns the executable JSON Schema. Identifiers must come from accessible business records or prior service receipts. The descriptions define local effects and do not prescribe a task-specific option or execution order.

### `propose_factoring_settlement`

Prepare an invoice-finance assignment, local obligation payment, net remittance or overadvance repayment.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `case_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `action` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
| `data` | object | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.
